reader.summary: 07-learning-from-corrections.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly stumble on the 25% sum in Step 2, which is worked out but never used, and on the wording "Say 8 sentences", which reads like an instruction.

history.summary: 07-learning-from-corrections.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly stumble on the 25% sum in Step 2, which is worked out but never used, and on the wording "Say 8 sentences", which reads like an instruction.
07-owning-a-mistake.html 9/10. A newcomer would mostly be unsure why the sorting game sits at the end of Step 3, and would want one concrete example for the claim that owning a mistake builds trust.
07-copying-formulas.html 8/10. A newcomer would most likely stall on where the formula goes in the practice task and on the $C$1 notation, which the lesson uses but never breaks down.
07-telling-a-story.html 8/10.

07-batching-small-tasks.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly stumble on the unexplained 5-minute restart figure in the worked example, which is presented as fact, and on the phrase "deeper work", which is only explained in an earlier lesson; the rest of the steps are clear.

07-keeping-records.html 9/10. A newcomer would follow the money maths without trouble; the snags are that the 'other is the largest' example does not match the numbers above it, and the sorting game has no instructions.
07-following-up-after-meetings.html 9/10.

07-deciding-together.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly wonder what the owner should do when their call goes against the group's view, because the lesson explains how to hear people but not how that fits with the owner's final say.
07-editing-your-draft.html 9/10.
07-writing-a-status-report.html 8/10.

07-writing-a-status-report.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly struggle with why money spent is compared with work done, and what the time number is for, since Step 2 only compares tasks and money with the plan.

07-writing-a-status-report.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the time-gone number, which is never worked out, and with deciding whether a line is on track, at risk or off track, because the lesson gives no rule for either.
